title: Activation Plateaus: Where and How They Emerge
entrypoint: full_experiment.sh (runs scripts/interpolate_and_record_activations.py plain / --freeze_attention / --freeze_mlp, then all scripts/*_plots.py and jacobians_*.py)
primary_claim: Activation plateaus in GPT-2 Large emerge and sharpen gradually across layers, are produced specifically by MLP blocks rather than attention blocks, persist without LayerNorm, and correspond to areas of high MLP input-output Jacobian sensitivity at their boundaries.
quote: activation plateaus emerge and sharpen gradually across model layers, with later layers having a slightly weaker—but similar—effect.
metric: relative (L2) distance of model outputs across activation-space interpolation, and component-freezing effect on plateau formation
target_value: freezing MLP block outputs completely eliminates plateaus; freezing attention block outputs has relatively small effect
tolerance_rationale: headline is not a single scalar; judge by hand

needed: none — uses a single hardcoded shared_context prompt ('The house was') and two hardcoded token pairs from config.yaml

inspector_notes: Cleanest and cheapest repo in this batch: small pretrained model, fully pinned dependencies (exact versions incl. CUDA build tags), no external data, and a single shell script (full_experiment.sh) reproduces the entire pipeline exactly as configured in config.yaml (model_name: gpt2-large).
headline_artifact: plots/ directory: step-size, relative-distance, and Jacobian plots comparing normal vs. attention-frozen vs. MLP-frozen interpolation runs (the 'freezing MLP eliminates plateaus, freezing attention does not' result)
